complete_historical_findings.body: [INFERENCE: static control-flow trace] With committed action 6 and a torn temporary reservation for 7, reserved_actions returns 7, but this caller only logs the audit. The next RHS attempts reservation 8 by truncating the same temporary file; if that publication is interrupted during the write, the committed counter remains 6 and the next recovery returns 7 again, losing one cumulative reservation. The audit does not prevent this because reserved_actions never reads telemetry. Commit the recovered count as the baseline, preserving its audit first, before permitting another RHS reservation. The smoke publishes the valid-temp recovery explicitly and never interrupts publication after a torn-temp recovery, so its passing checks do not cover this CLI sequence.

disposition.rationale: The helper invokes record_audit before touching the temporary evidence, publishes the recovered count through reserve_action, and returns only after publication succeeds. The CLI cannot enter the next RHS reservation before that committed baseline exists. Root's recorded second-partial-publication check changes from 7 before repair to the expected 8 afterward; interrupted baseline publication and failing audit callbacks are also covered by recorded passing checks.

complete_historical_findings.title: Commit the recovered counter before reserving another RHS action

complete_historical_findings.body: [INFERENCE: static control-flow trace] When required=True and both committed counter copies are absent, a leftover malformed .tmp starts from count 0, is charged as 1, and sets found=True, so the missing-accounting refusal is bypassed. The CLI uses required=True for a nonzero-time checkpoint and would then continue with an unknown historical action total treated as 1, defeating the cumulative cap. Keep committed-counter presence separate from temporary-file presence and refuse a required missing committed baseline before interpreting an ambiguous temporary reservation. The current smoke tests missing accounting only when the temporary file is also absent.

disposition.rationale: Only successfully decoded current/previous counters establish committed history. The required-history refusal now occurs before temporary-file recovery, so temporary presence cannot satisfy it. Root's recorded missing-baseline-plus-torn-temp case changes from incorrectly admitting 1 to the expected ValueError; existing corrupt committed-counter decoding still fails rather than falling through.

complete_historical_findings.title: Require a committed counter before accepting a torn temporary file
